newsitem.title: INDIA: India's GAIL to start petrochemicals plant in June.
newsitem.headline: India's GAIL to start petrochemicals plant in June.

text.p: The state-run Gas Authority of India Ltd (GAIL) expects to commission its petrochemical complex in June, its chairman and managing director said on Saturday.
"Hopefully production should begin by June," GAIL chairman and managing director C.R. Prasad told a conference on deepwater oil and gas exploration.

The $1.0 billion petrochemical complex at Auraiya in the northern Uttar Pradesh state will be India's second gas cracker. The first is that of state-run Indian Petrochemical Corp Ltd at Nagothane in western India.
The downstream plant will produce a 265,000 tonnes a year of polyethylene, Prasad said. He said GAIL had set up a countrywide marketing and distribution network to market plastics.
GAIL is India's leading marketer of natural gas, operating a 1,400-km (870 mile) long natural gas pipeline from the western coast to north India, feeding several industries along the way.
